question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q6b — U-235 Fission: Mass Totals and Energy Released
question.text:
The equation below represents a nuclear fission reaction utilized in power plants:

\({}^{235}_{92}\text{U} + {}^{1}_{0}\text{n} \rightarrow {}^{141}_{56}\text{Ba} + {}^{92}_{36}\text{Kr} + 3{}^{1}_{0}\text{n} + \gamma\)

Masses:

  • \({}^{235}_{92}\text{U} = 3.902 \times 10^{-25}\text{ kg}\)
  • \({}^{1}_{0}\text{n} = 1.675 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)
  • \({}^{141}_{56}\text{Ba} = 2.289 \times 10^{-25}\text{ kg}\)
  • \({}^{92}_{36}\text{Kr} = 1.575 \times 10^{-25}\text{ kg}\)

(i) Calculate the total mass of the particles on the left-hand side (reactants) and the right-hand side (products). (4 marks)

(ii) Calculate the mass difference. (2 marks)

(iii) Calculate the energy released. [c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹] (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q6b(i) — Total masses:
Reactants: m(U) + m(n) = 3.902×10⁻²⁵ + 1.675×10⁻²⁷ = 390.2×10⁻²⁷ + 1.675×10⁻²⁷ = 391.875 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 3.91875 × 10⁻²⁵ kg
Products: m(Ba) + m(Kr) + 3m(n) = 2.289×10⁻²⁵ + 1.575×10⁻²⁵ + 3×1.675×10⁻²⁷ = 228.9 + 157.5 + 5.025 = 391.425 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 3.91425 × 10⁻²⁵ kg

Q6b(ii) — Mass difference:
Δm = 3.91875×10⁻²⁵ − 3.91425×10⁻²⁵ = 0.00450×10⁻²⁵ = 4.50 × 10⁻²⁸ kg

Q6b(iii) — Energy:
E = Δm × c² = 4.50×10⁻²⁸ × (3.0×10⁸)² = 4.50×10⁻²⁸ × 9.0×10¹⁶ = 4.05 × 10⁻¹¹ J

steps.label:
Conversion tip: Express all masses in the same power (×10⁻²⁷ kg): U = 390.2, n = 1.675, Ba = 228.9, Kr = 157.5
Formula: Δm = m(reactants) − m(products)  |  E = Δm × c²
Q6b(i) — Calculate the total mass of reactants and total mass of products. (4 marks)
Q6b(ii) — Calculate the mass difference Δm. (2 marks)
Q6b(iii) — Calculate the energy released E = Δmc². (3 marks)
